Synopsis:
Banks and asset managers financing US data center construction are adding community/political opposition as a formal credit risk factor. Lenders (JPMorgan, Morgan Stanley, BofA) now require permits, approvals, and community support as preconditions before advancing project loans. As of Q1 2026, 75+ projects worth ~$130B face local opposition. Despite friction, financiers remain committed to the sector given Goldman's $6T+ AI capex forecast through 2030. Structural safeguards (covenant compliance, drawdown gates tied to permits) are being built into credit facilities to manage cancellation risk.
